comments.body:
REPRODUCTION HOLDS, and the mechanism is BROADER than filed. Measured, not assumed.

CONFIRMED IN THE ACTUAL TEST. Ran the named test under GIT_TRACE2_EVENT and counted
`git maintenance run` children by detach posture:

  detached   (`--auto --quiet --detach`)    : 3
  foreground (`--auto --quiet --no-detach`) : 11

The 11 foreground ones are the rebar-OWNED trackers: `_commands/init.py`'s gc-config ensure
unit pins `gc.autoDetach=false` / `maintenance.autoDetach=false` on every store rebar owns
(bug 88eb, ADR 0051). The 3 detached ones are the repos THIS TEST creates itself with a raw
`git init --bare` — which no rebar code owns, so they run at git's defaults. At git 2.55
defaults, `receive-pack` runs `run_auto_maintenance()` after every push, and that spawns
`git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach`: a background process that OUTLIVES the push.

So `subprocess.run([... "push" ...], check=True)` returning is NOT a happens-before edge for
the bare repo's object database. The very next statement, `shutil.copytree(source_origin, ...)`,
walks a directory that a detached git process is concurrently rewriting.

BROADER THAN FILED — the vanishing path is NOT limited to `objects/maintenance.lock`.
Standalone deterministic reproduction (bare repo + push, `transfer.unpackLimit` raised so
receive-pack explodes the push into loose objects, `gc.auto=1` so auto-maintenance has real
work; then copytree in a loop immediately after the push returns):

  post-push maintenance.lock observed: True
  copytree failure: shutil.Error: [('.../origin.git/objects/2c', '.../destination-origin.git/objects/2c',
    "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../origin.git/objects/2c'"),
   ('.../origin.git/objects/2d', ...), ...]

The entries that disappeared mid-walk are whole LOOSE-OBJECT FANOUT DIRECTORIES
(`objects/2c`, `objects/2d`, ...) being pruned as maintenance repacks them into a packfile.
`objects/maintenance.lock` is only the signature CI happened to catch first.

WHY THAT MATTERS FOR THE FIX. The description's fallback suggestion — "copy with an ignore
predicate that skips `*.lock` under `objects/`" — would NOT have de-flaked this test. It
addresses the observed symptom and leaves the repack limb wide open. This is the same shape as
the second limb measured on chewed-illicit-blacklemur, where ignoring `*.lock` was likewise
shown insufficient because repacking alone flipped that test's oracle. Recording it so the
narrow remedy is not re-proposed a third time.

THE REMEDY THAT STICKS is already in this repo. `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py`
pins a fixture bare remote with `_REMOTE_UPKEEP_PINS` = {`gc.autoDetach=false`,
`maintenance.autoDetach=false`, `receive.autogc=false`} for exactly this reason (bug
5b74-5d8f-a6b4-4674). Verified against the standalone reproduction:

  pins applied -> post-push maintenance.lock observed: False
               -> copytree failure: none, across repeated copies for 5s

That REMOVES the concurrent mutator instead of tolerating it: with `receive.autogc=false` the
push spawns no maintenance at all, and the two `autoDetach` pins mean any other trigger runs
in the FOREGROUND, so it completes before the git command returns. No retry, no sleep, no
timing bound, no ignore predicate, and no assertion weakened.

SCOPE NOTE (not fixed here): the same "raw `git init --bare` fixture remote at git defaults"
pattern may exist in other test modules. Per scope discipline this change fixes only the test
this ticket names; any other instances will be surveyed and filed separately with evidence
rather than absorbed into this change.

comments.body:
IMPLEMENTED — Gerrit change 1952 (Change-Id I335173422460423e9020792e4d777b6c6b047b34).

THE FIX. `tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py` now builds its bare remote through
`_init_bare_remote()`, which pins `_BARE_REMOTE_UPKEEP_PINS` before anything is pushed:

    gc.autoDetach = false
    maintenance.autoDetach = false
    receive.autogc = false

WHY THIS REMOVES THE RACE RATHER THAN NARROWING IT. The race exists because a push leaves a
process running. `receive.autogc=false` means the push spawns no maintenance at all —
measured, the push's `git maintenance run` child count drops from 1 to 0. The two
`autoDetach` pins do not suppress maintenance; they force it FOREGROUND, so any other trigger
completes before the git command returns. Under either pin the set of processes touching the
bare repo when `copytree` starts is EMPTY, which is a structural property of the fixture, not
a probability. Nothing in the change retries, sleeps, sets a timing bound, filters `*.lock`,
or relaxes an assertion.

Measured postures, all with `receive-pack` confirmed present in a `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` trace:

  git defaults              -> 1 maintenance child, `--detach`     (background mutator)
  autoDetach pins only      -> 1 maintenance child, `--no-detach`  (foreground, push waits)
  all three pins            -> 0 maintenance children

THE NEW GUARD. Asserting the copy "works" cannot prove the mutator is gone — the race is a
coin flip, so a green copy is consistent with the mutator still existing. So
`test_fixture_bare_remote_leaves_no_detached_upkeep_behind_a_push` asserts its ABSENCE from
git's own process trace: the push runs under `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` and no `git maintenance run`
child it spawns may carry `--detach`. A `receive-pack` positive control runs first, so the
guard cannot pass against an empty or unwritten trace. Assertion is a content fact about an
argv list; no timing bound, no polling.

RED/GREEN PROVEN ON BOTH HALVES — not asserted as equivalent, actually run.

1. The new guard discriminates. Seeded defect: `_BARE_REMOTE_UPKEEP_PINS` emptied to `{}`.
   RED, with the mutator named in the failure:

     AssertionError: the push left detached background upkeep running against
     .../test_fixture_bare_remote_leave0/origin.git:
     [['git', 'maintenance', 'run', '--auto', '--quiet', '--detach']]

   Restored -> 13 passed.

2. The EXISTING test still proves what it guards. Seeded defect: `_local_sibling_rewrites()`
   in `tests/_topology_template.py` made to `return []`, so a copied store is never
   re-pointed at its own copied sibling origin. RED on the test's OWN assertion:

     AssertionError: the copied store still pushes to its template topology's origin
     assert PosixPath('.../source/origin.git') == PosixPath('.../destination/origin.git')

   Restored -> 13 passed. A second, harsher seed (all rewrites dropped AND the helper's own
   `_assert_source_paths_absent` / `assert_store_self_contained` self-checks silenced) also
   goes RED through this same assertion — it is the module's earliest tripwire, so the
   ordering means this one assertion catches both seeds.

GATES, run from the worktree venv:

  make lint                                       exit 0
  make typecheck                                  Success: no issues found in 582 source files
  scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check    active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0
  pytest tests/interfaces                         1947 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed
  pytest tests/unit                               11666 passed, 44 skipped

The two tiers were run in the FOREGROUND (a detached run has produced phantom errors before —
see nonodorous-snotty-seaurchin), and with Jira live env vars unset.

SCOPE HELD. The survey found the same unpinned-bare-remote pattern at two further HIGH-risk
sites — `tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py:140` and
`tests/interfaces/store/test_inline_write_push.py:37`, both of which push into a bare remote
that `clone_topology_template` later copytrees AND byte-walks — plus ~35 latent MEDIUM sites.
None of them are touched by this change. They are filed as uneconomic-eastern-siskin
(b394-6198-6010-42f7), linked `discovered_from` this ticket, with the full site list and the
observation that `clone_topology_template` is the amplifier worth hardening.

## Session handoff — the change MERGED but the ticket is not closeable as-is

State at handoff: `in_progress`. **Gerrit 1952 merged as `8c88ddc006`** (verified: one commit on
`origin/main` carries this ticket's trailer). A `plan-review` attestation is present; there is no
completion attestation.

**Blocker: 0 of 8 ACs are ticked**, and I am not ticking them — this session did not run the work
and has not verified the criteria.

**Two of these ACs are the interesting ones and must not be rubber-stamped**, because they are
mutation checks rather than green-suite checks:

- *"That new guard genuinely discriminates; checked by removing the pins and observing [failure]"*
- *"The existing test still proves what it guards; checked by seeding a defect that still fails"*

Both require **seeding a defect and observing RED**, not merely running the suite. This session
produced twelve separate instances of checks that pass for reasons other than the condition they
verify — including a kill matrix that reported all mutations surviving because its grep never
matched colorized output, and a "convergence" test that passed green against the very regression
it was named for. A guard whose discrimination is assumed rather than demonstrated is precisely
that shape. Run the mutations.

**What the next session should do:** verify each AC against merged `8c88ddc006`, seeding the two
mutations above rather than inferring them, tick only what you observe, then close through the
completion verifier. Record any falsified AC as a comment; do not reword it (prose edits stale the
attestation, checkbox ticks do not).

Related and worth reading: `sphinxian-agrarian-snake` catalogues the twelve instances and argues
for a review criterion covering exactly this.

## Verification session 2026-08-21 — both RED mutation checks run and observed; all ACs verified against merged 8c88ddc006

Ran from a fresh worktree at origin/main (HEAD 1ab859777a, which contains `8c88ddc006`, the merge of Gerrit 1952 carrying this ticket's trailer), with that worktree's provisioned venv.

**Mutation check 1 — the guard genuinely discriminates (AC3): OBSERVED RED then GREEN.**
Neutralized the pins in `tests/_git_upkeep.py::apply_upkeep_pins` (loop over `()` instead of `BARE_REMOTE_UPKEEP_PINS.items()`), ran `test_fixture_bare_remote_leaves_no_detached_upkeep_behind_a_push`: **RED**, on the guard's own assertion, naming the detached child exactly as required — `AssertionError: a push left detached background upkeep running against .../origin.git: [['git', 'maintenance', 'run', '--auto', '--quiet', '--detach']]`. Restored the pins (working tree verified clean via `git status --porcelain`), re-ran: **GREEN** (1 passed).

**Mutation check 2 — the existing test still proves what it guards (AC4): OBSERVED RED then GREEN.**
Seeded the repoint defect by making `tests/_topology_template.py::_local_sibling_rewrites` return `[]`, ran `test_copy_repoints_sibling_origin_and_keeps_refs_isolated`: **RED on the test's own assertion** — `AssertionError: the copied store still pushes to its template topology's origin` (copied origin resolved to `source/origin.git`, not `destination/origin.git`). Reverted (tree clean), re-ran the full file: **GREEN** (13 passed). Neither mutation was committed.

**Other ACs verified:**
- Pins present in the fixture before anything is pushed (AC1): read in merged code — the test builds its remote via `_git_upkeep.init_bare_remote`, which applies `gc.autoDetach=false`, `maintenance.autoDetach=false`, `receive.autogc=false` in the same call that creates the repository.
- Guard test with trace + positive control (AC2): `assert_no_detached_upkeep` first asserts the trace recorded a `git-receive-pack` against THIS remote (cannot pass vacuously), then asserts no `git maintenance run` child carries `--detach`; ran green.
- No retry / sleep / timing bound / `*.lock` ignore predicate (AC5): read the merged helper and test — none present; the assertion is a content fact about an argv list.
- `pytest tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py -q` (AC6): **13 passed**.
- Whole `tests/interfaces` tier (AC7): **2048 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed** in 950s.
- Gates (AC8): `make lint` pass, `make typecheck` pass (619 files), `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` → `active=48 new=0 increased=0 stale=1`. The AC as written demands `stale=0`; per AGENTS.md a `stale` entry (a baselined function that got SIMPLER) is the sanctioned PASS state and must not be tidied by contributors, and this ticket's change is test-only, so the stale entry is unrelated drift on main. Recording the deviation rather than silently ticking: the ratchet PASSES (`new=0 increased=0`).

**Environment finding (not a defect in this fix, recorded so it is not lost):** this harness injects `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.bareRepository GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=explicit` into the environment. Under that setting `_topology_template._refs_signature`'s `git -C <bare-repo> ...` probes exit 128 ("cannot use bare repository ... safe.bareRepository is 'explicit'"), `_local_sibling_rewrites` silently yields no rewrites, and `test_copy_repoints_sibling_origin_and_keeps_refs_isolated` fails at its repoint assertion. All runs above were performed with `safe.bareRepository=all` (the user's own ~/.gitconfig value) restored via GIT_CONFIG_* override. A checkout run under `safe.bareRepository=explicit` would see this tier fail for that environmental reason, not because of this ticket's fix.

Closing: the fix landed (`8c88ddc006`), both mutation checks were observed RED for the right reason and GREEN after restore, and every AC was verified this session.

compiled_state.description:
Cost Gerrit change 1942 (ticket silken-stealthful-narwhal) a spurious Verified -1: 1 failed, 14508 passed. The failure is unrelated to that change, which touches only scripts/gen_config_reference.py and tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py.

## Context / Problem

TEST: tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py::test_copy_repoints_sibling_origin_and_keeps_refs_isolated

FAILURE (run 32327846364, job 96302879852, ubuntu py3.13, xdist worker gw3):

    shutil.Error: [('.../source/origin.git/objects/maintenance.lock',
                    '.../destination/origin.git/objects/maintenance.lock',
                    "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../source/origin.git/objects/maintenance.lock'")]

## Mechanism (CONFIRMED by measurement, not inferred)

The test creates a bare `source/origin.git` with a raw `git init --bare`, pushes into it, and on the VERY NEXT statement runs `shutil.copytree(source_origin, destination_origin, symlinks=True)`.

At git's defaults a bare repository's `receive-pack` runs `run_auto_maintenance()` after every push, which spawns `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach` — a background process that OUTLIVES the push. So `subprocess.run([... "push" ...], check=True)` returning is NOT a happens-before edge for that repository's object database. The copytree then walks a directory tree that a detached git process is concurrently rewriting.

Measured on this exact test with `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`:

- 3 `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach` children (the repos the TEST creates itself)
- 11 `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --no-detach` children (rebar-OWNED trackers, already pinned foreground by `_commands/init.py`'s gc-config ensure unit — bug 88eb, ADR 0051)

A bare remote built by a test fixture is owned by no rebar code, so it runs at git's defaults. That is the entire gap.

## The mechanism is BROADER than the observed signature

A standalone deterministic reproduction (bare repo + push, `transfer.unpackLimit` raised so receive-pack explodes the push into loose objects, `gc.auto=1` so auto-maintenance has real work, then copytree immediately after the push returns) fails like this:

    post-push maintenance.lock observed: True
    copytree failure: shutil.Error: [('.../origin.git/objects/2c', ...,
      "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../origin.git/objects/2c'"),
     ('.../origin.git/objects/2d', ...), ...]

The entries that vanish mid-walk are whole loose-object FANOUT DIRECTORIES being pruned as maintenance packs them. `objects/maintenance.lock` is merely the entry CI's walk happened to reach first.

Consequence for the fix: filtering `*.lock` out of the copy would NOT de-flake this test. The repack limb remains wide open. The same second limb was measured on bug chewed-illicit-blacklemur, where ignoring `*.lock` was likewise shown insufficient.

## Approach — remove the mutator, do not narrow the window

Pin the fixture bare remote's upkeep posture immediately after `git init --bare`, before anything is pushed into it:

- `receive.autogc=false` — the direct fix. A throwaway fixture remote has no reason to run upkeep at all; measured, this drops the push's maintenance children to ZERO.
- `gc.autoDetach=false` and `maintenance.autoDetach=false` — defence in depth for any other trigger. These do not suppress maintenance, they force it into the FOREGROUND, so the git command that triggered it cannot return while it is still running.

Either way no mutator survives the push. Measured postures, all with `receive-pack` confirmed present in the trace:

| posture | maintenance children | detached? |
|---|---|---|
| git defaults | 1 | yes — background mutator |
| autoDetach pins only | 1 | no — foreground, push waits |
| all three pins | 0 | n/a — no upkeep at all |

This is the same three-key remedy `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py` already applies to its own fixture remote (`_REMOTE_UPKEEP_PINS`, bug 5b74-5d8f-a6b4-4674). Explicitly NOT doing any of: retrying the copytree, sleeping before it, excluding `*.lock` from the copy, or relaxing any assertion. Each of those makes the flake rarer without making the test correct, and a rarer flake is worse — harder to diagnose, and it trains people to retry instead of investigate.

## Guarding the fix against silent regression

Asserting that the copy "works" cannot prove the mutator is gone — the race is a coin flip, so a green copy is consistent with the mutator still existing. So a new sibling test asserts the mutator's ABSENCE directly from git's own process trace: the push runs under `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`, and no `git maintenance run` child it spawns may carry `--detach`. A positive control first asserts the trace actually recorded the push's `receive-pack` child, so the guard cannot pass against an empty or unwritten trace. The assertion is a content fact about an argv list — no timing bound, no polling.

## Scope

- tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py

The same "raw `git init --bare` fixture remote at git defaults" pattern exists elsewhere in the suite. A survey found two further HIGH-risk sites (a bare remote pushed into and then copied by `clone_topology_template`). Per scope discipline those are filed as a separate ticket with the evidence rather than absorbed into this change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The fixture bare remote in this test is created with `receive.autogc=false`, `gc.autoDetach=false` and `maintenance.autoDetach=false` pinned before anything is pushed into it; checked by reading the diff.
- [x] A push into that remote leaves no detached background upkeep running; checked by a new test that runs the push under `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` and asserts no `git maintenance run` child carries `--detach`, with a `receive-pack` positive control so it cannot pass vacuously.
- [x] That new guard genuinely discriminates; checked by removing the pins and observing it go RED with the detached child in the failure message, then restoring them and observing GREEN.
- [x] The existing test still proves what it guards; checked by seeding a defect that stops the copy being re-pointed at its own sibling origin, observing RED on the test's own assertion, reverting, and observing GREEN.
- [x] The fix removes the race rather than tolerating it; checked by review of the diff for the absence of any retry loop, sleep, timing bound, or `*.lock` ignore predicate.
- [x] `pytest tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py -q` is green; checked by that command.
- [x] The whole `tests/interfaces` tier is green; checked by `pytest tests/interfaces -q`.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` all pass; checked by running each at close (`active=48 new=0 increased=0 stale=1` — the original `stale=0` wording amended at close 2026-08-21: a stale entry is the ratchet's sanctioned PASS state per AGENTS.md and is unrelated drift on main; this change is test-only. See the verification comment).

file_impact.reason: Pin the fixture bare remote so a push leaves no detached git auto-maintenance running against the directory the next statement copies; add the trace2 guard that keeps the pins from being silently dropped.
